content: 1. Strategies to improve iron status in toddlers were evaluated in a randomized controlled trial, as published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2009. The study demonstrated the effectiveness of specific interventions in addressing iron deficiency in this population. 2. Iodine-fortified toddler milk was shown to enhance dietary iodine intake and improve iodine status in toddlers, as evidenced by a randomized controlled trial published in the European Journal of Nutrition in 2020. 3. The consumption of whole milk and butter was associated with a clinically significant reduction in respiratory tract complaints in children, as reported in the Annals of Nutrition and Metabolism in 2015. 4. A public nutrition program that fortified milk with ferrous gluconate and zinc oxide successfully reduced the prevalence of anemia in toddlers, as detailed in the Journal of Nutrition in 2006. 5. A comparison of free amino acid content in standard infant formulas versus human milk was conducted, with findings published in the Journal of the American College of Nutrition in 2000. 6. The potential adverse effects of cow’s milk on children’s health were explored in a study published in the Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 2011. 7. A comprehensive review of the efficacy and effectiveness of nutrition interventions was conducted by Allen and Gillespie, published by the United Nations Administrative Committee on Coordination Sub-Committee on Nutrition in 2001. 8. Human breast milk’s composition and bioactivity were reviewed in detail, with findings published in Early Human Development in 2015. 9. Breastfeeding and bottle-feeding were identified as risk factors for dental caries in a systematic review and meta-analysis published in PLoS One in 2015. 10. The prevalence and impact of anemia in lowand middle-income countries were analyzed in a study published in The Lancet in 2011. 11. The GRADE guidelines for rating the quality of evidence were outlined in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011. 12. An introduction to meta-analysis methods was provided in a book published by John Wiley & Sons in 2008. 13. Early life protein intake and its sources, correlates, and tracking over the first five years of life were examined in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics in 2017. 14. The association between infant feeding modes and gastroesophageal reflux was analyzed in a study published in the Journal of Human Lactation in 2017. 15. The safety and nutritional aspects of soy-based infant formulas were reviewed in the British Journal of Nutrition in 2014. 16. The role of lipids in human milk and infant formulas was explored in a study published in Nutrients in 2018. 17. The effects of high milk intake on insulin levels and insulin resistance in children were reported in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2005. 18. The clinical course of cow’s milk protein allergy and atopic diseases in childhood was detailed in Pediatric Allergy and Immunology in 2002. 19. The nutritional and health implications of cow’s milk and goat’s milk were reviewed in the World Review of Nutrition and Dietetics in 2013. 20. The global strategy for infant and young child feeding was outlined by the World Health Organization in 2003. 21. The prevalence of anemia among children under five years of age was reported by the World Bank in 2017. 22. The impact of growing-up milk containing synbiotics on immune function and growth in children was evaluated in a study published in Clinical Medicine Insights: Pediatrics in 2013. 23. The role of lactose in enhancing mineral absorption during infancy was demonstrated in a study published in the Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 1983. 24. The adverse effects of cow’s milk in infants were discussed in the Nestlé Nutrition Workshop Series: Pediatric Program in 2007. 25. The risk of bias in observational studies was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool, which considers factors such as confounding, participant selection, intervention classification, and outcome measurement.
